newsitem.title: USA: Florida governor to propose $41 bln budget.
newsitem.headline: Florida governor to propose $41 bln budget.

text.p: Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles will propose a $41 billion budget this week, urging that spending rise by slightly more than last year's two percent increase, aides and published reports said Monday.
The state will have about $1 billion more to spend than this year, largely because tax revenues have grown with the robust economy.

Last year, the Democratic governor recommended a two percent increase in state spending, the smallest proposed increase in 20 years. Aides said this year's budget propsoal will exceed that two percent level.

Most of the increase would go to education and childrens' programs. Chiles will propose expanding subsidized daycare programs for welfare mothers who are trying to get off state assistance, and boosting the Healthy Kids program that provides low-cost health coverage for children of low income workers.
Chiles' budget will call for spending $121 million on economic development, a 14 percent increase over last year's $106 million allocation.
His proposal would give tax breaks to aircraft parts manufacturers and raise the state tourism marketing budget by $4 million.

His plan will also include a $6 million program that would pay bounties to agencies that find work for unemployed Floridians. Commmunity colleges and vocational schools would also receive bonuses for each student they train for high-paying jobs.
The Florida Legislature is under Republican control for the first time in 122 years. Lawmakers are scheduled to convene March 4.
Several bills affecting taxation and financing have already been filed.
HB3 would cut the tax businesses pay to cover unemployment insurance for workers. Florida has enough revenues to cover projected costs for three years.
HJR 51 would allow large counties to split their school districts. All districts are currently countywide.
SJR 4 would require a two-thirds vote instead of a simple majority vote in the legislature for bills that raise taxes.
Under HB15, welfare recipients who win more than $600 in lottery games would have the value of public assistance they have received over the last 10 years deducted from their winnings.

Two transporation groups, Floridians for Better Transporation and the Florida Transportation Commission, are urging lawmakers to increase gasoline taxes to fund highway and bridge improvements. A formal bill is still pending but preliminary discussions centered on raising the statewide gasoline tax by 5 cents, to 20 cents per gallon.
